newsitem.title: USA: Japan flexible on aviation talks with US - Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Japan flexible on aviation talks with US - Hashimoto.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told President Bill Clinton on Thursday that Japan will beflexible in bilateral aviation negotiations, a Japanese spokesman said.

"The prime minister told President Clinton that it is difficult to talk about the aviation issue if an open sky is the final goal...But Japan will be flexible in negotiations on issues including freight services," said the official who briefed reporters on the bilateral meeting of the two leaders ahead of the Group of Seven summit which starts here Friday.
U.S. Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater said earlier this week he would meet with his Japanese counterpart next Monday in Canada during an Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation ministerial meeting.
U.S. and Japanese officials have been meeting irregularly this year to try to resolve problems in their current air pact and set the stage for talks on a more liberal accord.
Clinton sounded flexible as well. The Japanese official quoted Clinton as saying that the U.S. is pursuing "open skies" liberal aviation accord but "a transitional period" could be considered.
Clinton was quoted as saying the U.S. wants to solve the dispute as soon as possible.
